sentences.t: The split tape.

The Dow closed up 0.85% at 50,018.70 on Tuesday - up 423 points, only six of its thirty names lower, Merck, Nike, Amgen and Salesforce all up more than 4% - while the S&P 500 fell 0.50% to 7,200.82, its eighth loss in nine sessions, and the Nasdaq composite dropped 1.48% to 23,733.54.
Nine of eleven S&P sectors rose; health care led at +2.97%, technology trailed at -3.26% (AP's close wire; the session's end-of-day table).
The bill lands on AI hardware.
Analog Devices fell 17.37%, the worst print in the S&P 500; Hewlett Packard Enterprise fell 16.33%; Dell fell 11.83% - all on earnings.
Nvidia gave back $9.67 to $155.38, down 5.86%, roughly $240 billion of market value (Nasdaq's closing record).
The gainers' table read like another market: Dollar Tree +11.18%, CoStar +8.08%, Moderna +7.21%.
Anthropic below its IPO price.
The model maker closed at $81.91, down 6.5% - under the $83 it priced at last week, in its fourth session since listing (Reuters/AFP wrap).
Asia's catch-up - and the hand-back.
Tuesday's closes: Taipei +8.99%, its largest single-day point gain on record; Seoul +6.32%, back above 5,000; Tokyo +3.91% after the long weekend.
This morning the chip names are giving it back: the Kospi opened down nearly 4%, SK Hynix and Samsung down about 6%.
The holiday deal's first tape.

Tata Steel sells its tubes and colour-coated businesses to APL Apollo for Rs 28,000 crore in cash, buys a 26.6% promoter stake at Rs 2,100 a share, and opens an offer for 26% more at Rs 2,301.40 - a combined 15.5-million-tonne platform targeted by 2035 (Tata Steel's release).
Both stocks trade on it for the first time today.
Nvidia's deadline.
The company's answers to the US Treasury on export-control compliance are due today (Politico); as of this morning nothing public has been filed.
Monday's reinstatement release disclosed a new national-security and export-control committee and a search for a chief compliance officer.
Mahanadi's allotment day.

Coal India's Rs 8,981-crore offer - subscribed 1.52 times final on the 49.31 crore shares open after the anchor book, carried by institutions at 4.95 times while retail stopped at 46% - allots shares today and lists Friday (PTI's final tally; Mint's guide).
America's data deluge.

October core PCE, the second estimate of Q3 GDP, jobless claims and durables all land tonight, compressed before Thanksgiving (the preview calendar) - after consumer confidence jumped to 103.3, its highest since January 2025, and ADP's weekly pulse showed hiring decelerating.
Mumbai reopens.
Equity and equity derivatives trading resumes after Prakash Gurpurab Sri Guru Nanak Dev.
The early marker flipped overnight: GIFT Nifty quoted up 1.22% at 2:44 AM, then down 0.26% at 5:42 AM, implying an open near 25,284 - a moving quote, not a prediction (the pre-market quote).
Tuesday on Wall Street was two markets.
The Dow closed at 50,018.70, up 0.85% - a 423-point gain with only six of its thirty names lower; Merck, Nike, Amgen and Salesforce each rose more than 4%.
The S&P 500 closed at 7,200.82, down 0.50%, its eighth loss in nine sessions, and the Nasdaq composite at 23,733.54, down 1.48%; the Russell 2000 added 0.57% to 2,684.94.
Nine of eleven S&P sectors rose - health care +2.97% led, technology -3.26% trailed.
The ten-year Treasury ended at 4.903%; the VIX at 26.36 (AP's close wire; the end-of-day tables).
The whole session in one line: the old economy up, the AI complex down.
The reversal stopped being about one stock.
The day's earnings broke across the AI-hardware shelf: Analog Devices -17.37%, the worst print in the S&P 500; Hewlett Packard Enterprise -16.33%; Dell -11.83%.
Nvidia gave back $9.67 to close at $155.38, down 5.86% - about $240 billion of market value gone in a day, after Monday's 31.5% reinstatement rally (the NVDA close record; CNBC's session report).
The top of the gainers' table belonged to another economy entirely: Dollar Tree +11.18%, CoStar +8.08%, Moderna +7.21%.
The bill for the AI build-out is landing on the companies selling the picks and shovels, not on the rest of the tape.
Anthropic's fourth session since listing closed at $81.91, down 6.5% - below the $83 it priced at last week (Reuters/AFP; Investopedia's session notes).
The market just had its best day since April and its newly public model maker has not caught a session of it.
Asia's catch-up, and the morning hand-back.
Tokyo's Nikkei closed Tuesday at 58,644.63, up 3.91% - 2,207.98 points against Friday's close, with the Topix up 2.47%, its first rise in six sessions (Jiji).
Seoul's Kospi closed at 5,006.03, up 6.32%, back above 5,000 (Yonhap).
Taipei's Taiex closed at 40,122.35, up 8.99% - a 3,310.46-point gain, the largest single-day point gain on record (Focus Taiwan's report).
The Hang Seng fell 0.73%.
Then Wednesday's open handed part of it back: Nikkei -0.45%, Kospi -3.94%, with SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics down about 6% (yicai's open flash, 8:02 AM Shanghai).
Tuesday was Asia digesting Monday's Wall Street rally; this morning is Asia digesting Tuesday's.
The holiday deal.

While Mumbai was closed, Tata Steel and APL Apollo's promoters signed a comprehensive agreement (owning release, dated Sunday-Monday): Tata Steel sells its Steel Tubes business (1.7 MTPA) and Tata Steel Colors (800 KTPA) to APL Apollo for Rs 28,000 crore in cash; it buys a 26.6% promoter stake in APL Apollo at Rs 2,100 a share - Rs 15,510 crore; and it makes an open offer for a further 26% at Rs 2,301.40 a share - Rs 16,756 crore.
A separate MOU with SG Tech Engineering (SG Spectra, a promoter-associated entity) covers 5 MTPA of colour-coated contract manufacturing, the first million tonnes within 24 months.
The target: 15.5 million tonnes of combined capacity by 2035 - about 9 in tubes, 6.5 in colour-coated - with closing inside FY2027, regulatory approvals pending.
CEO T V Narendran and CFO Koushik Chatterjee front the release.
Both stocks trade on it for the first time today.
Nvidia's deadline.
The company's answers to the Treasury on export-control compliance are due today, November 25 (Politico's report).

Treasury Secretary Bessent says his department is in touch with Nvidia's temporary management and lead directors and needs answers; Nvidia's Monday release disclosed the board's new National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee and a chief-compliance-officer search (the committee release).
As of 5:51 AM IST nothing public has been filed - a filing, a statement, or silence, each is a story.
Mahanadi's allotment day.

Coal India's Rs 8,981.12-crore offer - a pure offer for sale through which Coal India divests a 10% stake, priced at Rs 129-136 - closed subscribed 1.52 times on the 49.31 crore shares open to bidders after the Rs 2,295-crore anchor book: qualified institutions 4.95 times, retail 46%, non-institutional 66%, employees 22%, shareholders 56%.
The QIB book carried it; the retail and employee books went under-filled.
Allotment is expected today, demat credit Thursday, listing Friday on BSE and NSE (PTI's final tally; Mint's allotment guide).
America's data deluge.
Tonight brings October core PCE, personal income, the second estimate of Q3 GDP, weekly jobless claims and durable goods, compressed ahead of Thanksgiving (the calendar).

It lands on a split read: Conference Board consumer confidence jumped to 103.3 in November, the highest since January 2025, with the improvement concentrated among Democrats and independents after the midterms (Haver; CNBC), while ADP's NER Pulse put private hiring at +21,000 a week over the four weeks to November 7 - decelerating (ADP's release).
Mumbai reopens today after Prakash Gurpurab Sri Guru Nanak Dev; Monday's expiry close is the last official print: Sensex 82,435.99 (-1.77%), Nifty 25,349.65 (-1.75%), through the 25,500 support.

The trade-setup reads going in: Nifty resistance 26,000 with supports around 25,000 (HDFC Securities' Nagaraj Shetti); Nifty support 25,230-25,200, then 25,050, and Bank Nifty support 62,000-61,900 with the hurdle at 63,000-63,100 (SBI Securities' Sudeep Shah; both via NDTV Profit's trade setup).
The early marker flipped overnight.
GIFT Nifty quoted up 1.22% at 2:44 AM, then down 0.26% at 5:42 AM - an implied open near 25,284, about 66 points under Monday's close (the pre-market quote, last checked 5:51 AM IST).
A moving pre-market quote, quoted as one.
Monday's flows: foreign investors bought Rs 5,673 crore in the cash market, a sixteenth straight buying session; domestic institutions sold Rs 2,760 crore (CNBC-TV18; the flows table).
Provisional exchange tallies, revisable.
Overnight markers, from ABC's markets live blog (~4:15 AM IST): Brent +2.1% to $91.20 and WTI +2.2% to $81.89 - three more vessels struck in the Strait of Hormuz.
Spot gold -1.9% to $3,562 an ounce as Fed rate-hike expectations firmed.
Copper -4.8% to $11,912, a 13-month low.
Bitcoin -2.6% to $59,675.
The US ten-year quoted at 4.85% in Asia's morning against the 4.903% close.
Asia's Wednesday open: Nikkei -0.45%, Kospi -3.94%, the chip names - SK Hynix, Samsung - down about 6% (yicai).
Into that tape, tonight's US data lands with the consumer holding and hiring cooling: confidence at 103.3, ADP's weekly hiring pulse at +21,000 and decelerating.
Which of those tonight's core PCE print speaks to is the session's question.
Mahanadi Coalfields allots today.

The Rs 8,981.12-crore pure offer for sale - Coal India divesting a 10% stake, price band Rs 129 to Rs 136 - covered up to 66.18 crore shares in all, of which 49.31 crore were open for subscription after the Rs 2,295-crore anchor book; those closed at 1.52 times final subscription: QIB 4.95x, retail 46%, NII 66%, employees 22%, shareholders 56%.
Demat credit is expected Thursday, listing Friday on BSE and NSE; status checks run through BSE, NSE and KFin Tech (PTI's final tally; Mint's allotment guide).

Timed for the week: SEBI's Monday advisory cautions investors against relying on the unregulated grey-market premium - the GMP - quoted around upcoming IPOs, a market it notes is unregulated (SEBI's advisory).
Read alongside a retail book that stopped at 46% subscription, the regulator's point lands plainly.
No session on Tuesday, so Monday's board remains the live verdict going into today's reopen - percentages computed from BSE's official closes against Friday:

What moves it next: the reopen lands between tonight's US data deluge and Nvidia's Treasury deadline, with the Tata Steel-APL Apollo agreement getting its first tape and GIFT Nifty's overnight flip - +1.22% at 2:44 AM, -0.26% at 5:42 AM - pointing at a soft open.
All four open watchlist lines on the setup board closed red on expiry Monday; the board's next scored session is tonight.

Hindalco reappointed Satish Pai as managing director and named Mahindra Logistics chief executive Hemant Sikka deputy managing director effective 4 January 2027, with the India business transitioning progressively to him (Monday's exchange filing, via Mining Weekly).
The Tata Steel-APL Apollo agreement is on the front page.
Results today: Siemens Energy India reports Q2 FY27 (the results calendar).
The seesaw.
Gold fell 1.9% to $3,562 an ounce overnight because Fed rate-hike expectations firmed; Brent rose 2.1% to $91.20 because three more vessels were struck in the Strait of Hormuz (ABC's markets blog).
The two classic hedges moved in opposite directions - one pricing interest rates, the other pricing geopolitics.
When the Fed turns hawkish the metal pays the bill; when the Gulf heats up crude collects it.
Watching which force wins is the week's cleanest macro tell.
Term of the day: open offer.
When an acquirer crosses 25% of an Indian listed company, SEBI's takeover code requires an open offer to public shareholders for at least 26% more.

Tata Steel's structure shows both prices side by side: 26.6% of APL Apollo's promoter stake bought at Rs 2,100 a share (Rs 15,510 crore), then an open offer for 26% at Rs 2,301.40 (Rs 16,756 crore) (the release).
The offer price sitting above the stake price is the code's floor mechanics at work - public shareholders get the regulated exit, promoters got the negotiated one.
The other end of the complex.
Copper fell 4.8% to $11,912, a 13-month low - the growth metal voting slowdown while oil votes disruption.
In the US the consumer is holding (confidence 103.3, the highest since January 2025) while hiring cools (ADP's +21,000 a week, decelerating).
Tonight's core PCE decides which of those reads the Fed hears loudest.
Deadline day.
Nvidia's answers to the Treasury on export-control compliance are due today (Politico).

The questions outlived the boardroom crisis that prompted them: Jensen Huang is eleven days removed and reinstated, the board has a new national-security and export-control oversight committee, and a chief compliance officer is being hired (the committee release).
As of 5:51 AM IST, nothing public has been filed.
The two poster names.
Since Monday's reinstatement rally, the AI trade's most-watched pair has moved against the market's relief: Nvidia -5.86% Tuesday to $155.38, Anthropic -6.5% to $81.91, below its IPO price.
The money leaving the complex is not going to cash - it went to health care, up 2.97% on Tuesday, and to discount retail.
Richard Thaler's observation from casino studies: people treat winnings as a separate, less precious account than their own money, and take bigger risks with it - playing with house money.

This week wrote the phenomenon across the tape: a 31% single-day gain in the market's biggest name was, within a session, being treated as chips on the table rather than capital - easy come, easy sold.
The useful discipline is that there is no house money: every rupee in the account is equally yours, whichever day it arrived.
Tuesday was the market's holiday, so Monday's scored board stands as the live card - tonight's session is the next one scored.
Expiry Monday took all four open watchlist lines red: Kotak's trigger never threatened, ONGC's coil intact, JSW Steel's reward-to-risk still failing the screen, Hindalco's Friday reclaim undone.

The overnight wrinkle is crude: three more Hormuz strikes took Brent up 2.1% to $91.20, so the ONGC line - eight straight sessions under the 228 breakout, coil floor 218.50 intact - gets its ninth test with oil spiking.

The ledger is unchanged: HCLTech, filled 28 October at the worst fill of Rs 1,378.00, target Rs 1,466.80 taken out at 1,468.00 - gross +6.53%, net +6.23% after the 0.3% cost convention - last printed Rs 1,363.00 on Monday (+1.94%).
Infosys, resolved by invalidation, no trade, no P&L, last printed Rs 1,104.10 (+0.70%).
Research, not advice.
A setup activates only if the zone fills before any prior-day trade at or below the stop; a stop touched first kills the line before entry.
Entry is assumed at the worst price inside the published zone, not the best.
Reward-to-risk is computed from the worst fill to the published stop and target; lines that fail stay on the watchlist, not the board.
A line leaves the board only by stop, target or invalidation - never by opinion.
Mumbai reopens after the holiday; the Tata Steel-APL Apollo agreement gets its first tape.
Mahanadi allots (tentative).
US: October core PCE, personal income, Q3 GDP second estimate, durables and claims.
Nvidia's Treasury deadline.
Siemens Energy India results.
NYSE closed for Thanksgiving.
Mahanadi demat credit (tentative).
US 1:00 PM ET close.
Mahanadi lists on BSE and NSE (tentative).
India's Q2 GDP on 30 November; the RBI's MPC on 4 December; the Fed on 9 December; whatever Nvidia files or tells the Treasury; Anthropic's first full week.

Sources read for this edition: AP's close wire for the US indexes, with point moves reconciled exactly to Monday's closes; the session end-of-day tables for sectors and single-stock moves; Nasdaq's closing record for NVDA; CNBC's Nvidia session report; Reuters/AFP via CNA and Investopedia for Anthropic; Jiji for Tokyo's close, Yonhap for Seoul's, Focus Taiwan's report for the Taiex record; yicai's open flash for Asia this morning; ABC's markets live blog for the overnight markers; Haver and CNBC for consumer confidence; ADP's own media centre for the hiring pulse; Tata Steel's own newsroom release for the APL Apollo agreement, with every deal figure from it; Mining Weekly for the Hindalco board changes; SEBI's own advisory on grey-market premia; PTI and Business Today for Mahanadi's final subscription, Mint for the allotment mechanics; NDTV Profit's trade setup for the analyst levels; CNBC-TV18 and the flows table for FII/DII; the pre-market quote page for GIFT Nifty.
US closes are final-close wires or exchange end-of-day tables.
India prices are BSE's official bhavcopy prints; with no session Tuesday, Monday's prints remain the latest, and the top-movers board reprints Monday's chart as the live verdict.
GIFT Nifty and Asia's Wednesday moves are morning quotes as of roughly 5:50 AM IST and will move; they are quoted as markers, not predictions.
One wire's Tuesday US quotes were intraday and were not used as closes.

Mahanadi's Rs 8,981.12-crore issue size is the whole offer as the wires report it, anchor book included; the 1.52 times subscription is computed on the 49.31 crore shares open to bidders after anchors, and the retail figure follows the PTI and Business Today tally (46%) - Mint's reads 48%.
Each figure is printed as sourced, never blended.
This is research, not advice.

The Dixon long read carries one reporting-convention note: the Q2 profit figure appears in coverage as net profit of Rs 343.7 crore (ET, citing the exchange filing) and as consolidated PAT of Rs 411 crore; the long read prints the first, attributed, and the margin figures, which agree in both tellings.
That's the paper for Wednesday.
Mumbai reopens to a split tape, a Rs 28,000-crore deal's first trading, an allotment and an answer due in Washington.
See you tomorrow.
